title: Even electron count shortcut
statement:
A neutral atom or monatomic ion has an even number of electrons. What can you conclude before drawing orbital boxes?

[_]{a}

choices: It could be diamagnetic or paramagnetic.
It must have one unpaired electron.
explanations: Even count alone does not determine pairing.
A p² subshell supplies a counterexample.
Ferromagnetism involves collective ordering in material.
Exactly one unpaired electron would make the total odd.

hints: Pairing consumes two electrons at a time.
Even totals can still have multiple unpaired electrons.
solution: Pairing consumes two electrons at a time. Even totals can still have multiple unpaired electrons. A specific configuration is needed. Even count alone does not determine pairing.
